effect_estimate.comment: Deterministic simulation model calibrated to secondary case-study scores; no statistical regression estimates, confidence intervals, or p-values are reported.
effect_estimate.value: Across the 5 empirical case-study locations, water service delivery (WSD) performance scores were low: 20.0% to 26.6% of maximum performance in Kenya (Old Town 3/15 = 20.0%, Migosi 4/15 = 26.6%, Kangemi 3/15 = 20.0%; average 23.3%) and 13.3% to 20.0% in Ghana (Madina 2/15 = 13.3%, Nima 3/15 = 20.0%; average 16.6%). Calibrating the 12-month agent-based model (ABM) to these averages yielded C = 1.6 in Kenya (total simulated payoff = 61 under initial defection vs. 67.0 under initial cooperation) and C = 1.8 in Ghana (total simulated payoff = 56.9 under initial defection vs. 61.9 under initial cooperation), showing that social ties/power asymmetries outweigh third-party participation. In both countries, opportunistic management under low transparency, accountability, and participation (TAP) and asymmetric power produces Prisoner's Dilemma mutual-defection (Dd) equilibria with lower WSD performance payoffs than pragmatic management under balanced power, which produces Snow Drift (Cd/Dc) equilibria.
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 4, Section 'At the consumption level'; Table 5, PDF p. 7; PDF p. 9, Section 'Agent-based model (ABM) calibration'; Table 7, PDF p. 11; PDF pp. 11-12, Results & Overall Discussions and Conclusions

mechanism_certainty.comment: Rated 1 (design ceiling <= 2 because risk_of_bias_tool is NONE): the paper presents descriptive secondary empirical data across 5 case-study sites pairing weak integrity/TAP rules and opportunistic or pragmatic management with low WSD performance scores (13.3%-26.6%), while the specific strategic mechanism linking TAP/social ties to WSD payoffs (Prisoner's Dilemma vs. Snow Drift equilibria) is generated via a deterministic NetLogo simulation model rather than directly observed or quasi-experimentally tested in primary fieldwork reported in this paper.
